finalText:
I've made the new **Ideas** canvas (`.design/ui/Ideas.tsx`). It has one 1080 × 1350 concept poster for each of the five stickies in the GitPanel board's Ideas section. All five are dark, with a big headline, a one-line pitch and a small mock-up of the idea. Each one uses a different colour from the design system.

| Artboard | Sticky | Poster |
|---|---|---|
| `season-posters` | A dark-mode poster set for the season | "The season, after dark." Three fixture posters, each with a glowing amber moon |
| `match-recap` | A one-page match recap template | "Ninety minutes. One page." Score of 2–1, a goal timeline and three stat bars |
| `logo-sting` | An animated logo sting for reels | "Three seconds of us." A five-frame strip of the logo animating, with keyframes |
| `sponsor-wall` | A sponsor wall that updates itself | "Thank you, live." A grid of sponsors with a "synced" status and a just-added tile |
| `volunteer-signup` | A volunteer sign-up landing page | "We need you on matchday." A browser mock-up listing open shifts and a sign-up button |

I took a screenshot of each artboard and looked at it, and the canvas passes its check. One thing behaves differently from what the studio suggests:

- **The design system's colours and fonts are imported in the file itself.** The check suggests removing that import because the studio is meant to load it. When I removed it, the screenshots came out unstyled (no colours, a serif fallback font). With the import back, all five posters render correctly. GitPanel imports it the same way. This means the canvas keeps the maude look even if it's switched to another design system later.

Some content is invented and needs your real details: the fixture dates, the 2–1 score, the sponsor names, the shift counts and `club.example/volunteer`.

I didn't change the GitPanel board or its stickies, and I skipped the optional design review.
